name: Roan Taylor

education.notes: Placement/gap year (year 3) was spent building the startup. One year remaining.

currentSituation.primary: Building a SaaS startup that has landed its first paying customer.
currentSituation.treatment: High-EV bet AND a deep apprenticeship in how the startup world actually works. Not yet betting life on it.
constraints: One year of BEng to finish
Based in Northern Ireland — small ecosystem, planning to leave for some years
No safety net of a trust fund — financial freedom has to be earned
strengths: Already past one of the hardest filters: someone paid him money at 21
Well-read on startup ecosystem (Paul Graham, YC patterns)

northStar: A personal wealth engine — enough recurring income or savings to be free to do what he wants (travel, food & drink, learn deeply) — while doing meaningful work that creates real value for real people.
currentQuestion: What should I optimize for in the next 2-3 years to maximize the probability of reaching financial freedom + meaningful work by my early 30s — while keeping all three paths (Builder / Hustler / Founder) open as long as possible?

consideringPaths.description: Senior IC role at a great tech company (Anthropic, Stripe, Figma, deep-tech startup). High pay, real engineering, lower variance.
VC / accelerator / deal-driven role. Investment fluency, founder network, optionality.
Build his own company. Probably not the current startup — more likely a second attempt with sharpened domain insight.

operatingPrinciples: Don't bank life on the startup yet — finish the degree.
Use 21-24 to tip-toe down all paths — width before depth.
Elite branding is currency (Cambridge MPhil, top internship name, known company on CV).
Read history in 3D not 2D — decode mechanics, not headlines.
Get out of NI for some years (London / Cambridge / SF / Singapore).
Until ~24: optimize for learning rate. From 24: income + optionality. From 27+: ownership.
Domain insight > raw talent. Best founders are 22-24+, not 19-20.
Enjoy being young (PG's law). Exploration, character, worldview — not just résumé.

currentHypothesis.year1_now_to_mid_2027: Finish degree + scale or sunset startup. Goal: 5-10 paying customers. Apply to Cambridge MPhil (primary) + Oxford/ICL backups for 2027 entry as optionality. Apply to elite tech + VC internships for summer 2027.
currentHypothesis.year2_mid_2027_to_mid_2028: Width. Branch A: Cambridge MPhil + summer at top VC + side-building. Branch B: Full-time on startup if it hit threshold (£200k+ ARR). Branch C: Full-time elite seat (Builder at Anthropic/Stripe OR Hustler at Index/Atomico/EF). Get out of NI regardless.
currentHypothesis.year3_mid_2028_to_mid_2029: Commit. By 24, pick Builder, Hustler, or Founder with conviction from 3 years of width behind.

openQuestions: Founder survival rates at age 21-22 — what fraction reach financial freedom by 30
Credential vs experience — Cambridge MPhil vs top internship + full-time
Geography — can each path work from London, or do some need SF/NYC
The off-ramp if startup dies — what 'Plan B' jobs do failed founders take
Trader vs tech compounding over 15 years (Merricks-style elite-employee vs founder path)
Which tech companies + VCs have the best 'alumni-become-founders' track record
emotionalAnchor: Wants to look at his close friend (just landed £150k commodity-trader role at Merricks Capital, rotating Singapore/London/Mozambique/Brazil at age 20) and feel PROUD of him — not jealous — because Roan is confident and focused on his own path. The tool's success is measured by groundedness, not just analytical accuracy.
